result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days, and all four supplier listings plus the single-supplier lookup return them. The full suite passes: 610 tests, 0 failures.

What changed:
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the demo and existing call sites compile unchanged.
- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier.payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`DataStore.java`**: create and update write the terms. `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read them.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests. One follows the Swedish example (45 days, renegotiated to 14, checked in every listing and the lookup). The other checks the 30-day default.

Not done: other reports that build `Supplier` objects from their own queries (purchase suggestions, supplier performance, spending, supplier products) still go through the 5-argument constructor. They will show 30 days even when the supplier has other terms. Making them select the column is a small follow-up if those reports should show the real terms. I also left the demo output unchanged. Nothing is committed.
